referenceText: Every morning I walk to the small bakery at the end of our street. The owner, a quiet man with flour on his sleeves, always asks whether I want the usual. I nod, and he wraps a warm loaf of rye bread in brown paper. On the way back I pass the old library, where a few students are already waiting for the doors to open. The air smells of rain and coffee. By the time I reach home, the city is fully awake: buses rumble past, children laugh on their way to school, and somewhere a dog barks at nothing in particular. These ten minutes are the calmest part of my day, and I try not to waste them.
